messages:
From: James Park <j.park@globexcorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 14:12:00 -0400
Subject: Pilot procurement question: export compliance info and pricing

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement here at Globex would like to move forward with a 6-month pilot (50 seats, hosted) but we need a few things clarified before we raise a PO:

- Can Redwood provide written confirmation of export control compliance (ECCN/commodity classification) and whether any of the models or runtime components are subject to U.S. export restrictions?
- We need a sanctions screening and KYC check performed on Globex and our beneficial owners (we can provide the attached KYC spreadsheet).
- Pricing: your AE quoted a pilot discount of 35% off list for the pilot. That is above the typical floor our procurement team approves; if you need executive approval for non-standard discounts, please escalate.
- Data handling: Globex requires a clause preventing re-export and a statement on where inference compute and customer data will reside.

I attached the proposed SOW (Globex_SOW_Draft_v2.pdf) and our KYC form (Globex_KYC_Form.xlsx). Can you confirm next steps and an expected timeline for compliance checks?

Best,
James Park

Team,

Quick summary after a first pass with Security and Ops:

- Sanctions screening: initial screening by Sigma Compliance (attached) flagged a sub-entity of Globex that has historic dealings in APAC defense contracts. That alone does not automatically prohibit a deal, but it elevates us to "enhanced due diligence." We need completed KYC for beneficial owners and a written confirmation of end-use from Globex.
- Export controls: some of our model components use dependencies that are controlled for certain countries. We need Legal to confirm whether the runtime artifacts we're shipping (Docker images, model weights) fall under ECCN controls; short of that, we should implement an addendum forbidding re-export and restricting hosting regions.
- Commercial: Deal Desk policy — discounts >25% require VP Sales approval; discounts >30% require Sales VP + CFO approval. The requested 35% therefore needs escalation to Rishi and finance.

Recommendation:
1) Approve a conditional 25% pilot discount now to keep momentum.
2) Require Globex to sign the export_control_addendum and complete the KYC spreadsheet within 5 business days.
3) Run a third-party sanctions verification (Sigma Compliance) and hold on any on-prem or cross-border compute until cleared.

I’ve attached the preliminary sanctions_screening_report.txt and a draft export_compliance_addendum.pdf for Legal to review.

-Vivek
Head of Deal Desk Ops
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Pilot procurement question: export compliance info and pricing — legal redlines

Team,

I reviewed the SOW and the proposed addendum. Key items and my position:

- Export/compliance: I’ve redlined language requiring the customer to warrant that they will not use Redwood services for prohibited military end-uses and to indemnify Redwood for breaches of export controls. We should add a clause that explicitly forbids re-export without prior written consent.
- KYC/Screening: Require Globex to complete the KYC spreadsheet and provide government-issued IDs for UBOs over 10% ownership if requested. Third-party sanctions screening must be completed before any production data access.
- Data residency: Given the risk profile, do not allow on-prem or cross-border provisioning during the pilot. Hosting must be in US regions only unless Security signs off.
- Commercial: For the 6-month pilot, Legal will accept up to a 25% discount without further escalation. Any discount above 25% requires written approval from VP Sales. Discounts >30% require CFO sign-off and an exec escalation memo.

I attached the redlined SOW (SOW_redlines_Globex.docx) and my proposed export_compliance_addendum.pdf. If we need to move to 35% for strategic reasons, obtain an exec memo from Sales outlining strategic value and risk mitigations.

-Aisha Rahman
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Compliance
Redwood Inference

1) Approve a 25% pilot discount (for the 6-month pilot) effective immediately so Marissa can keep the deal moving.
2) Require Globex to complete the KYC form and for Sigma Compliance to sign off on the sanctions screening within 5 business days.
3) Globex must sign the export_compliance_addendum and accept US-only hosting during the pilot; no on-prem or cross-border compute until explicit Security/Legal sign-off.

Marissa: you have a conditional approval for 25% — please communicate these conditions to James and request the completed KYC and signed addendum. I’ll loop Finance if they push for anything beyond 25%.
